title: Teable
name: teable
description: Spreadsheet-style database in the vein of Airtable, built on Postgres: grid, kanban, calendar, gallery and form views, file attachments, formulas, real-time collaboration and an API. Source: https://github.com/teableio/teable

env.name: TEABLE_SECRET
env.label: Secret key (required)
env.description: Signs logins and encrypts stored tokens. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: TEABLE_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Letters and numbers only, since it goes into a database URL. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: TEABLE_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on
env.description: Like http://192.168.1.10:3500. Invite links and profile pictures point here, so they break on any other address.

env.name: TEABLE_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the secret key and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The first start sets up the database and takes a couple of minutes, then open http://<your-host>:3500 (or whichever port you picked). The first account you sign up becomes the admin. Anyone who can reach it can sign up after that, so once you're in, switch off Allow creating new accounts under System Admin --> Instance settings. Set the address field to wherever you'll open it, or invite links will point at localhost. Teable's image sends a small daily usage report to Teable (your instance ID, how many people are active, and a rough count of spaces and bases). To stop it, add TEABLE_TELEMETRY_OFF set to true to the stack's environment variables and redeploy. AI features and enterprise extras need a paid licence, everything else is free. Attachments live in the teable-data volume, logins in teable-cache, and your tables in postgres-data. Docs: help.teable.ai
